messages.subject: Devtools 1.4 release candidate
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We have a release candidate for devtools 1.4. Please install, test it out, and let us know if you run into any problems!

To install it on Mac and Linux, please run:
  devtools::install_github('devtools', 'hadley', ref='v1.4-rc')
And then you may need to restart R afterward.

To install on Windows, please follow the instructions at:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/7106772

Here's the changes from the NEWS file:

## Installation improvements

* `install()` now respects the global option `keep.source.pkgs`.

* `install()` gains a `build_vignettes` which defaults to TRUE, and ensures
  that vignettes are built even when doing a local install. It does this
  by forcing `local = FALSE` if the package has vignettes, so `R CMD build`
  can follow the usual process. (#344)

* `install_github()` now takes repo names of the form `username/repo` -
  this is now the recommended form for install_github if your username is
  not hadley ;)

* `install_github()` now adds details on the source of the installed package
  (e.g. repository, SHA1, etc.) to the package DESCRIPTION file. (Thanks to JJ
  Allaire)

* Adjusted `install_version()` to new meta data structure on CRAN.
  (Thanks to Kornelius Rohmeyer)

* Fixed bug so that `install_version()` works with version numbers that
  contain hyphens. (Thanks to Kornelius Rohmeyer)

## Other minor improvements

* `build(binary = TRUE)` now no longer installs the package as a side-effect.
  (#335)

* `create_description()` does a better job of combining defaults and user
  specified options. (#332)

* `install()` also installs the dependencies that do not have the required
  versions; besides, the argument `dependencies` now works like
  `install.packages()` (in previous versions, it was essentially
  `c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo")`) (thanks, Yihui Xie, #355)

* `check()` and `check_cran()` gain new `check_dir` argument to control where
  checking takes place (#337)

* `check_devtools()` no longer incorrectly complains about a `vignettes/`
  directory

* Decompression of zip files now respects `getOption("unzip")` (#326)

* `dev_help` will now use the Rstudio help pane, if you're using a recent
  version of Rstudio (#322)

* Release is now a little bit smarter: if it's a new package, it'll ask you
  to read and agree to the CRAN policies; it will only ask about
  dependencies if it has any.

* `source_url()` (and `source_gist()`) accept SHA1 prefixes.

* `source_gist()` uses the github api to reliably locate the raw gist.
  Additionally it now only attempts to source files with `.R` or `.r`
  extensions, and gains a `quiet` argument. (#348)

-Winston

messages.subject: Using install_github and roxygen2
messages.body_plain:
Hello, it seems that to use devtools::install_github to obtain a functioning package install the repository must also have changes in man/ and NAMESPACE that are made by roxygen2::roxygenize() to your package source tree.

This also means that in order to obtain the built vignettes, the inst/doc/ folder must be pushed as well, after the package is built to a tarball and then untarred (or the equivalent to the standard R CMD workflow).

I'm confused about the vignette part, since devtools::document and devtools::build make the NAMESPACE and man/*.Rd but the built vignettes end up in the tarball (as per standard R CMD workflow).

How do committed devtools/github users maintain their mixed source/built projects so that users get a fully-functioning installation with install_github? I see that https://github.com/hadley/lubridate contains the inst/doc/ built files, but it's not clear to me how the build/install workflow results in the mixed source tree.

I use roxygen2 for the man/ and NAMESPACE, but I prefer to keep those out of GitHub - I can see the need to push them out, but surely the staging/commit process is pretty untidy, and the vignette process escapes me.

I'd appreciate any pointers to where this is explained or notes on how people build their workflow to suit.

Thanks, Mike

messages.subject: Re: Error: Command failed (1)
messages.body_plain:
I believe this is a problem specific to installing devtools on Windows. On windows, you can't overwrite an open file. Devtools, however, includes a DLL which is loaded (and open) while devtools is loaded. So when you try to install a new version of devtools on top of your currently-loaded version, it fails.

There are some ways around this. I believe this should work: build a binary package for devtools with `build('devtools', binary=T)`, restart R so that devtools isn't loaded, and then install the binary package.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Devtools 1.4 release candidate
messages.body_plain:
There's one more last-minute feature we've just slipped into devtools 1.4 RC. There's now a new function, `build_github_devtools()`, which makes it much easier for Windows users to install the development version of devtools. From now on, Windows users will be able to upgrade to the github version of devtools with:

    library(devtools)
    build_github_devtools()

    #### Restart R before continuing ####
    install.packages("./devtools.zip", repos = NULL)

    # Remove the package after installation
    unlink("./devtools.zip")

-Winston
